foot_carpet.note: 03: brown noise burst 70 ms, LP 900 Hz, soft attack. Heel then a softer toe 55 ms later, a low body thump, a faint fabric scuff.

foot_tile.note: 03: white noise click 20 ms + sine 1.8 kHz 15 ms, HP 400 Hz. A hard heel click with a ceramic tink under it (1.8 kHz plus an inharmonic 2.9 kHz plate mode) and a little body, then the toe. Click and tink ring longer than the table (35 ms, 90 ms) so the step carries the -14 dB walk level of 03 §6 rule 1 without crushing the click.

foot_water.note: 03: tile step + noise band 2 kHz / 1.5 kHz bandwidth 120 ms with a ripple envelope; louder than dry steps. A low plunge and three rising bubble chirps make it read as water rather than hiss.

foot_concrete.note: 03: noise burst 40 ms, BP 1.2 kHz, short tail. Gritty heel, a low knock, a sandy scuff, the toe, and an 11 ms slap off the nearest pillar.

foot_raised_floor.note: 03: concrete + hollow resonance sine 180 Hz 60 ms. Two panel modes (180, 291 Hz) and a small double rattle as the tile settles in its frame.

foot_substrate.note: 03: tile click + 1 kHz square blip 10 ms, bit-crushed. The steps sound synthetic: identical heel and toe blips, 6-bit, held to 12 kHz.

sprint_breath_loop.note: 03: pink noise shaped by a 0.9 Hz LFO, LP 1.5 kHz. Exhale (darker, louder) and inhale (brighter, softer) as two shaped phases of the 0.9 Hz cycle; 4 breaths per loop under a slow random depth so no two breaths match. AudioManager fades it in over 2 s of sprinting.

stamina_empty_gasp.note: 03: breath burst 400 ms, HP 300 Hz. A sharp inhale whose formant rises (1.3 to 2.4 kHz), an airy hiss over it, a throat-catch at the onset.

crouch.note: 03: cloth rustle, pink noise 150 ms, BP 2 kHz. Crinkle grains (random AM at 70 Hz) over a soft low whoosh of the body moving. Plays down and up.

flashlight_toggle.note: 03: relay click, square 2.5 kHz 4 ms + noise 10 ms. Snap, a plastic housing resonance, and the spring's second click 12 ms later. Also the relay click in ui_title_boot.

crank_loop.note: 03 crank loop, ratchet part: a 12 Hz click train (square 3 kHz 3 ms) with a noisy tick, a pawl knock, and a gear grind turning at the same 12 Hz. The whine is crank_whine, a separate loop, so its pitch can follow charge without speeding up the ratchet.

crank_whine.note: 03 crank loop, whine part: a dynamo whine rendered at 450 Hz so pitch_scale 0.444 to 2.0 covers 200 to 900 Hz; a soft second harmonic and a 12 Hz flutter tied to the crank's turning.

crank_full.note: 03: the click train stops; one bright click 5 kHz. A ringing ting so it reads as 'full', over a small clunk.

noclip_charge.note: 03: sine cluster (3 detuned sines, 110 Hz) rising to 440 Hz over the charge + a rising bit-crushed noise band. Rendered at 220 Hz so pitch_scale 0.5 to 2.0 sweeps 110 to 440 Hz with the charge; the crushed band and a 6 Hz scanline shimmer rise with it.

noclip_commit.note: 03: sub thump (45 Hz decaying 250 ms) + digital tear (white noise through an 8-bit crush, 120 ms) + a 60 ms silence gap. The gap runs 20 to 80 ms, inside the 80 ms hitstop: the impact, then the frozen world is silent, then the tear resumes as the pass begins.

noclip_fall.note: 11: the floor commit plays noclip_commit plus a falling sine during the 1.2 s black: 600 to 55 Hz with a slow wobble, over a closing wind band.

noclip_fail.note: 03: short descending sine 300 to 120 Hz, 150 ms, dull (low-passed, no transient). Also the invalid-target tone (11).

noclip_cancel.note: 06 §8 and 11: releasing early cancels with a short descending tone as the preview collapses (100 ms). Softer than noclip_fail, with a trace of the charge's crushed band.

drop_arrival.note: 11 arrival (drop): a sub settle as black and grain give way to the new level, with a low rumble and a little crushed grain.

coherence_loss_tick.note: 03: 1.2 kHz square blip 8 ms; played per Coherence point lost, rate-limited to 20 Hz.

coherence_gain.note: 03: warm chord, sines 220/330/440 Hz, 600 ms, soft. Strummed 15 ms apart, each voice a detuned pair for warmth, a whisper of triangle for body, low-passed.

heartbeat.note: 03: two sine thumps 55 Hz (90 ms, 70 ms) spaced 180 ms; AudioManager retriggers it at 60 to 140 bpm by threat. Each thump drops in pitch around 55 Hz; soft saturation adds the 110 Hz harmonic so small speakers still carry it.

error_contact_hit.note: 03: the noclip commit tear at 2x length (240 ms) + sub 40 Hz + a 1 s decaying noise band at 400 Hz. The bite.

dissolve.note: 03: the static bed to full, a pitch-dropping sine cluster, 1.5 s, cut to silence (3 ms anti-click only).

ui_move.note: 03: 2 ms noise tick, HP 4 kHz (the 2 ms fade-in rule makes it a 6 ms tick). Also the item-select tick (11).

ui_slider_step.note: 03: tick with pitch by value; a short 1 kHz body under the tick so pitch_scale is heard as pitch. 12: each settings slider plays it at the new level.

ui_glitch_transition.note: 03: 120 ms bit-crushed noise swipe; sliced at ~90 Hz like the 8 to 14 bands, swept 6 kHz to 800 Hz and panned left to right.

ui_title_boot.note: 03: 1.5 s rising sine cluster + relay click + hum settle. The cluster climbs an octave over 1.25 s, the relay closes, the 100 Hz hum takes over and settles away.

ui_unlock.note: 03: sine 660/990 Hz 200 ms, dry. The fifth arrives 50 ms after the root; no reverb.

ui_summary_stamp.note: 03: thud + paper. A rubber stamp landing (knock and low thud), then the sheet shifting under it.

ui_shutter.note: 04 §4: every motion has its sound. The shutter's six bands at 10 ms offsets, as six falling micro-ticks alternating left and right.

ui_type.note: 04 §4: typing at 60 characters per second; a barely-there tick, rate-limited by the caller.

ui_hold_tick.note: 11 interact hold: a low tick every 0.2 s while the prompt's underline fills.

noclip_pass_wall.note: 11 noclip commit (wall): the 250 ms pass after the commit's gap. A pressure whoosh swept up through the wall's thickness, a crushed grid crackle (the unrender lines within 3 m), and a low ring as the far face opens.

noclip_pass_soft.note: 09 soft wall: the cheap pass through a shimmering wall. Lighter than the wall pass: an airy shimmer (30 Hz flutter like the wall's shimmer) over a short falling glide, no sub, no crackle.

room_tone_halls.note: 03 §1 place: the Halls room tone, carpet-damped. A dark brown-noise body (the building), carpet-absorbed air with no highs, the bank of 120 Hz tubes far down the corridor, and a slow random swell so the loop does not breathe audibly. 03 §6 rule 3: AudioManager never ducks it below -40 dB.

fixture_hum_halls.note: 03 fixture hum loop, Halls colour: brighter, 120 Hz fundamental with 240 Hz at -12 dB and a faint pink-noise air; a thin ballast buzz on top. Mono: one per fixture, started by the fixture with AudioManager.start_loop.

fixture_buzz_halls.note: 03 Halls fixtures, buzz colour: a tired tube whose ballast buzzes. A band-passed 120 Hz saw with a 120 Hz rattle and a slow irregular level, over the same hum. Some fixtures carry it instead of fixture_hum_halls; it is not Flicker's stutter (that is gated at 8 to 20 Hz with clicks).

room_tone_pools.note: 03 §1 place: the Pools room tone, a tiled hall with water in it. Hard surfaces keep the air bright: a thin brown-noise body, a hiss band around 2 kHz off the tiles, a slow wash (water moving somewhere out of sight), the panels' 100 Hz far off. The bus reverb (room 0.9, wet 0.45, 40 ms predelay) does the size. 03 §6 rule 3: never ducked below -40 dB.

fixture_hum_pools.note: 03 fixture hum loop, Pools colour: the ceiling panels, a clean 100 Hz with 200 Hz at -12 dB and a cool, airy pink noise; no ballast rasp (the tiles would throw it everywhere). Mono, one per lent light.

fixture_buzz_pools.note: 03 Pools fixtures, buzz colour: a tired panel ballast, a band-passed 100 Hz saw with a slow irregular level over the hum. Steady; not Flicker's stutter.

water_lap.note: 03 water lap loop (Pools): pink noise band-passed at 600 Hz under slow random envelopes, a softer 1.4 kHz slap layer on its own slower envelope so the two never line up. Mono: one per wet basin, at the water (WaterVolume).

drip.note: 03 drip: a sine at 2.2 kHz dropping in pitch over 60 ms (the drop's bloop) and a tiny splash of filtered noise; a faint second plink as the ripple settles. Cosmetic, no caption (not an error or door event).

room_tone_garage.note: 03 §1 place: the Garage room tone, a concrete deck open to the night somewhere. A low brown rumble (traffic far away, through the slab), a dry concrete air band at 500 Hz, the sodium lamps' 60 Hz bed and a slow swell like wind through the ramps. 03 §6 rule 3: never ducked below -40 dB.

fixture_hum_garage.note: 03 fixture hum loop, Garage colour: a sodium lamp, 60 Hz with 120 Hz at -12 dB and a fine crackle (sparse high clicks of the arc). Mono, one per lent light.

fixture_buzz_garage.note: 03 Garage fixtures, buzz colour: a sodium lamp near the end of its life, a rough 60 Hz saw band and a heavier crackle over the hum, slowly swelling. Steady; not Flicker's stutter.

room_tone_offices.note: 03 §1 place: the Offices room tone, a dead office floor. Air handling through the ceiling (a soft pink-noise wash band-passed round 700 Hz under a slow swell), the carpet and the drop tiles eating the highs, and the troffer bank's 100 Hz with its 50 Hz buzz far off. Drier and closer than Halls (the bus reverb is room 0.4, wet 0.15). 03 §6 rule 3: never ducked below -40 dB.

fixture_hum_offices.note: 03 fixture hum loop, Offices colour: a troffer, 100 Hz with 200 Hz at -12 dB and a faint pink-noise air, and the 50 Hz buzz under it (03: Offices 100 Hz with 50 Hz buzz). Mono, one per lent light.

fixture_buzz_offices.note: 03 Offices fixtures, buzz colour: a troffer ballast going, a band-passed 50 Hz saw rattle with a slow irregular level over the 100 Hz hum. Steady; not Flicker's stutter.

room_tone_server.note: 03 §1 place: the Server room tone, a cold room full of machines. A dense even wash of cooling air (brown and pink noise, a broad 400 Hz body), the units' faint high whine (a 5.2 kHz sine pair beating slowly, very low), and the mains 60/120 Hz of the power supplies. Steadier than the other strata: machines do not breathe. The bus reverb is small and dead (room 0.3, damping 0.8). 03 §6 rule 3: never ducked below -40 dB.

fixture_hum_server.note: 03 fixture hum loop, Server colour: what a lent light carries here is the rack beside it (the LED aggregate) or an emergency box: a power supply's 120 Hz with a thin coil whine high above, and a little fan air. Mono, one per lent light.

fixture_buzz_server.note: 03 Server, buzz colour: a supply with a failing fan, the 120 Hz hum with a rough band-passed saw and a slow irregular level. Steady; not Flicker's stutter.

fan_loop.note: 03 fan loop (Server): brown noise low-passed at 500 Hz with a 23 Hz rotor amplitude modulation, a touch of blade hiss above. Mono: one per ceiling fan grille (ServerFan).

power_wave_ignite.note: 03: power wave fixture ignite, ballast tink (sine 4 kHz 8 ms) + hum fade-in 300 ms, per fixture; AudioManager hashes the pitch +-5% from the fixture's position. The hum hands over to the fixture's hum loop.

door_open.note: 03: latch click, then the wood creak (saw 80 Hz FM'd by 0.5 Hz, 300 ms). Stick-slip grain (random AM) through a hinge resonance makes the saw read as wood.

door_close.note: 03: a short creak, the latch click, and the thud (sine 60 Hz 120 ms) of the door meeting its frame.

door_slam.note: 03: the door's thud at three times the gain, with a short room reverb pre-baked. A fast whoosh of the swing, the frame impact, the latch rattling in its keeper.

breaker_lever.note: 03: heavy relay, square 150 Hz 20 ms + metal clank (noise BP 3 kHz 40 ms) + sub 50 Hz. The handle's travel, the contacts closing, the panel ringing briefly.

exit_open.note: 03: exit elevator / stairwell door, a long hydraulic hiss (noise LP 2 kHz 1.5 s) + heavy latch + fixture tink. 11: enter exit and exit unlocked.

exit_latch.note: 11: the exit's heavy latch alone, for exit seen (Open, Powered, Keyed) and the Cycled seal and unseal.

exit_tone.note: 07 Cycled lock: the long tone from the exit 5 s before it opens, max_distance 60 m, heard through walls. 11: also the exit-seen tone for a Cycled exit. A plain 196 Hz tone with a soft octave, slow swell and fall.

static_hum.note: 03 Static: hum loop, 50 Hz + 100 Hz sines with slow beating (each a pair 0.5 Hz apart). Soft saturation adds 150 and 250 Hz so the hum carries on small speakers. Heard through walls to 40 m. The noise band is static_band, a separate loop whose gain the field raises.

static_band.note: 03 Static: the white-noise band at 3 kHz whose gain rises inside the field (the Static code sets its volume on the loop handle). A fast irregular crackle in it so it reads as interference, not air.

still_tick.note: 03 Still: the render-line tick, a 6 kHz blip 10 ms, with the 1 px line (02 §8) after 2 s of observation.

still_contact.note: 03 Still: on contact, a single sine 30 Hz 2 s, played with error_contact_hit. A touch of saturation adds 60 and 90 Hz so it is felt and heard.

echo_breath.note: 03 Echo: within 4 m, a breathing-length noise swell every 2 s (its only sound besides the player's own footsteps played back). Pink noise, LP 1.2 kHz with a soft 600 Hz body, a slow rise and a long fall; no voice, no pitch.

item_pickup.note: 03 item pickup: a short glass tick at 3 kHz, then a confirm sine at 660 Hz for 80 ms. The tick is a high sine with a fast exponential decay, the confirm a soft-edged tone with a quiet octave above.

note_pickup.note: 03 note pickup: paper slide, pink noise high-passed at 2 kHz for about 200 ms. A rising swell as the sheet is dragged, a dry flick at the end.

polaroid_charge.note: 03 Polaroid use, part one: the camera flash charging, a whine rising from 1.4 to 4.2 kHz over 0.3 s with a faint inductor buzz under it. The shutter is polaroid_shutter, played on the flash.

polaroid_shutter.note: 03 Polaroid use, part two: the shutter clack on the flash frame. A bright snap, a spring body, the blade closing 45 ms later, and the flash capacitor's short pop of noise.

glowstick_crack.note: 03 glowstick crack: a plastic snap (noise, 10 ms) with a second smaller snap as the vial breaks, then a short burst of chemical fizz (pink noise, high-passed at 4 kHz). The sustained fizz is glowstick_fizz.

glowstick_fizz.note: 03 glowstick: the chemical fizz loop, pink noise high-passed at 4 kHz, very quiet (about -30 dB under the crack), heard only within a few metres. Gentle crackle bursts keep it alive.

glowstick_land.note: 09 §2 landing of a thrown glowstick (the 6 m impact noise): a light plastic tap on the floor, a dry knock with a short hollow ring.

chalk_mark.note: 03 chalk mark: three short scrapes (noise, band-pass 5 kHz, 60 ms each), the middle one a touch louder, each with a grainy attack.

flare_ignite.note: 03 flare ignite: a strike (noise scrape, band-passed 3 kHz, 120 ms) and a hiss as the cap catches, then the first of the sustained roar (brown noise BP 800 Hz with crackles; the roar itself is the flare_burn loop).

flare_burn.note: 03 flare: the sustained roar, brown noise band-passed at 800 Hz, with crackles (short white-noise bursts above 2 kHz at random).

flare_land.note: 09 §2 landing of a thrown flare (the 6 m impact noise): a heavier knock than the glowstick, a paper-and-wax tube on concrete, with a short rattle.

radio_static.note: 03 radio static loop: white noise band-passed around 1 to 3 kHz with a slow wobble. The item sets the loop's gain from the exit alignment (09 §2): noise when away, swelling as the player faces the exit.

radio_ping.note: 03 radio ping: a 1 kHz sine for 50 ms with a soft edge, repeating faster as the player faces the exit.

fuse_insert.note: 03 fuse insert: a metal slide (noise, band-passed 2.4 kHz, 220 ms), the seating click, then the hum starting (120 Hz fading in).

fuse_pull.note: 09 §2 fuse pulled back out: the click first, then the slide, and the hum cut.

keycard_accept.note: 03 keycard reader accept: a 1.5 kHz beep for 100 ms.

keycard_reject.note: 03 keycard reader reject: two beeps at 400 Hz.

vending_hum.note: 03 vending machine: a compressor hum, 100 Hz sine with 200 Hz at -10 dB and a faint 50 Hz rumble.

vending_whir.note: 03 vending machine on use: a mechanical whir for 1 s (a saw at 90 Hz rising, ratcheting) ending in the thunk of the item dropping into the tray.

payphone_ring.note: 03 payphone: the ring, two sines at 440 and 480 Hz modulated at 20 Hz, 2 s on. The phone plays it every 6 s (2 s on, 4 s off) while ringing. Heard through the walls: the point is that it is heard.

payphone_line.note: 09 §5 payphone answered: two seconds of an open line, a 60 Hz hum under thin pink noise and a faint far tone. Nothing speaks.

hide_locker.note: 11 §2 locker: the door closing with a click, a tin thud and the latch.

hide_under_car.note: 11 §2 under car: a scrape of cloth and grit on concrete as the player slides under, a low bump of the belly.

hide_under_desk.note: 11 §2 under desk: a chair-leg scuff and the soft knock of a knee on the modesty panel.

hide_pump_corner.note: 11 §2 pump room corner: the room door swinging shut on its closer, the latch, and a pipe ticking.

hide_rack_gap.note: 11 §2 rack gap: a shoulder brushing a steel rack frame, and the faint ring of a drive tray.
